## The failure, and the trap under it

Two errors, one file, adjacent lines — every other job on `e0d3160` is `completed: success` (TypeScript Type Check, Test Core ×3, Dogfood ×3, Temporal Conformance, Build Core/Docs, Check Changeset, Validate Package Dependencies):

```
packages/qa/dogfood/test/federated-rls-injectors.dogfood.test.ts
  83:5  error  slot-lookup/no-any-assignment
  84:5  error  slot-lookup/no-any-assignment
```

**⚠️ Why this passed locally and failed on the runner** — worth recording, because the obvious next move is the wrong one. The code carries

```ts
// eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any
const kernel = stack.kernel as any;
```

but CI runs **`eslint . --no-inline-config`**, so **inline disable comments are inert on the runner**. Re-adding or adjusting a disable comment would fail again in exactly the same way. The patch instruction says so explicitly and points at the rule's own prescribed fix instead: pass each slot's real contract type rather than erasing the lookup.

Also carried into the instruction: the rule's message states that *every* `any` it has caught so far was hiding a real gap — so if honest typing makes the compiler object, **that is a finding to report, not something to cast away.** Making ESLint quiet is not the deliverable; keeping the test meaningful is.
